answer: Enrollment issues each agent a unique birefringent glass coupon. At a public bench, a registered prism and a sealed reference mirror photograph the coupon's stress fringes under polarized light; that pattern is the identity. Every renewal must be shot outdoors on a logged night, and the same hour's gale has to shift the fringes in step with the official weather record. A copied photo fails the live wind-coupled test, and a sybil farm cannot share one coupon—each fake identity needs its own ground glass, fixture, and weather-matched recapture, so cost scales with the herd.
